name: flood-mark
title: Flood Mark
description: A threshold-setting control drawn over its own history: the last 30 days plot as a braille dot field and you drag a horizontal ─── rule up and down through it, with every day above the rule flipping live from a muted dot to a solid foreground ▴ and a fixed line stating exactly what that setting would have cost — 'would have fired 3 times last month', broken down per week.
useWhen: configuring an alert threshold where the person setting the number needs to see the noise it would have produced against real history before committing, not just type a value into a bare field — drag a rule through a braille plot of the last 30 days and read the alert count it implies. Pick meter-threshold-trip instead when the threshold is already fixed and you're watching a live value latch against it (no authoring), or gauge-capacity-waterline when the only thing that matters is the current fill against one static line — flood-mark is the one case where the threshold itself is the thing being dragged and history is what you interrogate with it.
instruction: Renders `history` (an array of daily samples, ideally 30, oldest first) as a braille-dot scatter field and a draggable horizontal rule — the flood mark — that sets a threshold value against it. FIELD: ROWS=8 stacked bands of braille cells span the field's fixed height; each day's value maps to one of ROWS*4 quantized vertical slots via the left column's 4 addressable dot bits (dots 1/2/3/7, top-to-bottom, U+2800 + bit), so each day renders as exactly one single-dot braille glyph at the row/sub-row its value rounds to — a real 2D scatter of history, not a bar chart. RULE: a full-width row of '─' glyphs sits at a CONTINUOUS y position (unmixed with the field's ROWS*4 quantization) computed straight from the live threshold value against the same min/max domain, with a small mono tag ('{value}{unit}') riding its right end and a grab-dot ('●') at its left end that recolors to --ns-accent only while actively being dragged (never at rest, never on hover — accent is interaction-only) — everything else on the rule is --foreground/--border/--background tokens. COMPARISON: every render, each day's raw value (not its quantized dot slot) is compared directly against the live threshold — days above it ('would have fired') cross-fade their single-dot glyph to a solid foreground '▴' via two stacked absolutely-positioned spans toggling opacity 0/1 on a 150ms transition, with transition-delay = min(240, round(|value-threshold|/domain * 8) * 30)ms, so a big threshold jump visibly ripples outward from the rule's new position rather than flipping every day in lockstep; drag and arrow-key stepping both drive this identically since it's derived purely from render-time value comparison, not a separate animation trigger. CONSEQUENCE: below the field, a line reads 'would have fired {N} times last month — wk1 {c} · wk2 {c} · ...' (history chunked into 7-day weeks) — the number is never shown without its per-week retrospective cost. DETENTS: p50/p95/p99 of `history` render as faint muted tick marks off the field's left edge; dragging soft-snaps the raw pointer value to any detent within 2% of the domain, and Shift+ArrowUp/Right (or Shift+ArrowDown/Left) jumps straight to the next detent above (or below) the current value, falling back to an ordinary `step` move past the top/bottom detent. INTERACTION: the entire field (not just the rule strip) is one role=slider node, tabIndex=0, aria-orientation=vertical (the value axis IS vertical here, even though the glyph itself is a horizontal line), aria-valuemin/max from the real metric domain, aria-valuenow=current, and aria-valuetext carrying the full consequence sentence ('threshold 480ms, 3 alerts in the last 30 days') rather than the bare number — pointerdown anywhere in the field jumps the rule there and begins a drag (pointer capture on the same node), ArrowUp/Right and ArrowDown/Left step by `step`, Home/End go to the domain rails. The consequence paragraph is `role=status aria-live=polite` and doubles as the only live region — since `commit()` only actually updates state when the quantized value changes, a drag doesn't spam re-announcements every pixel, only at each real step. The braille field and the detent ticks are `aria-hidden` and `pointer-events-none` (decorative; the slider node carries all real semantics and pointer handling); the rule's visual row (dashes, grab-dot, value tag) is also `aria-hidden` since it's drawn purely from state already exposed via aria-valuetext. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` collapses the cross-fade transition and its ripple delay to 0ms; the rule's own position never animates (it tracks the live value directly, no tween). Colors are token utility classes only — text-foreground, text-ns-muted (plus /0 and /50 and /80 opacity variants), border-border, bg-background, text-ns-accent for the two interaction-only spots — no hex, no canvas, DOM+CSS only.
